summary:
All words have length `L`, so a chain starting at `i` is made of the chunks at `i, i + L, i + 2L, …`. Group the
start positions by `i mod L`; within one group, slide a window over consecutive chunks with a count per word.
Grow by one chunk; shrink from the left while that word is over-used; reset after an unknown chunk. A window of
exactly all words is a match. O(n · L) chunk work instead of O(n · words · L).

question.md:
`words` all have the same length. Return every index of `s` where some ordering of all the words (with their
multiplicities) appears concatenated.

- **s up to 10⁴**, **up to 5000 words**, word length up to 30.

think.md:
`s = "catdogcatcatdogdog"`, `words = ['cat', 'dog']` → **[0, 3, 9]**.

Checking a start means cutting `2` chunks and comparing word counts. Neighbouring starts that differ by `L`
share all but one chunk, so they belong to the same sliding window. Starts at different offsets mod `L` never
share chunks, so we run `L` independent windows, each stepping one whole word at a time.

idea.md: For each start, cut `w` chunks and compare their counts with the word counts.

lines.text: Word length, number of words, and how many times each word is required.

notes.c: Give each distinct word an id, and precompute the id of the chunk starting at every position (−1 if it isn't a word).

lines.text: Sort the words, merge duplicates into counts, and binary-search each chunk of `s` among them.
Every start where a full chain fits.
Count the chunks; any chunk used more often than required (or unknown) rules this start out.

notes.c: Undo the counts after each start instead of clearing the whole array.

complexity.md: **Time O(n · w · L)** (cutting and hashing `w` chunks per start). **Space O(w · L).**

walk.title: Every start i: cut s[i : i + 6] into 2 pieces of 3 letters and compare their counts with the word list.

limits.md: Starts `L` apart share almost all chunks, but each is checked from scratch.

approaches.title: One word-sized window per offset

idea.md: For each offset `0..L−1`: walk chunks `j = off, off + L, …`. Unknown chunk: reset. Otherwise count it; while it's over-used, drop the window's first chunk. When the window holds `w` chunks, record `left` and drop its first chunk. Sort the results.

build: Grow by a word, shrink on overuse, reset on unknown.

notes.c: Ids for the distinct words and for the chunk at every position.

lines.text: Sort the words, merge duplicates into counts, and binary-search each chunk of `s` among them.
Starts with the same remainder mod `L` share chunks; each offset gets its own window.

notes.c: Before the next offset, undo the counts still held by this window.

lines.text: Take the next whole word into the window.
An unknown chunk can't be in any chain: empty the window and start after it.
This word is now used too often: drop words from the left until it isn't.
Exactly all words: a chain starts at `left`. Drop the first word to keep looking.
Offsets interleave, so sort the starts.

complexity.md: **Time O(n · L):** each offset walks `n / L` chunks, each hashed in O(L), and every chunk enters and leaves once. **Space O(w · L)** for the word table.

walk.title: Words start at multiples of 3 from some offset 0..2. For each offset, slide a window over whole words with word counts; shrink when a word is over-used or unknown.

takeaways.md:
- **Fixed-length tokens:** split the starts by offset mod `L` and slide over whole tokens.
- Shrink on over-use, reset on an unknown token.
- Same idea as anagram windows, with words instead of letters.
